input: Draft a scholarship application essay for my masters program

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Scholarship essays vary widely — some ask 'Why do you deserve funding?', others ask 'Describe your research goals' or 'Explain financial need.' The specific prompt determines every word of the essay.
The essay must reflect the user's actual background, achievements, and identity — without knowing their academic/professional story, the draft will be generic and unconvincing.
The field of study and program name shape the vocabulary, angle, and examples used — a STEM essay reads very differently from a humanities or policy one.
Most scholarships impose a strict word or character limit; writing 1,200 words when 500 are allowed means the entire draft needs restructuring.
The deadline determines urgency and how many revision rounds are feasible; it also affects how polished the first draft needs to be.
Tone can range from formal and academic to personal and narrative-driven. The user may want to lead with a story, a mission statement, or data — this shapes the entire structure.
Knowing what the scholarship committee prioritises (financial need, academic merit, leadership, community impact) tells us what to emphasise and what to leave out.

gold.taskTitle: Draft a Masters Scholarship Application Essay
gold.taskDescription: Write a compelling scholarship application essay to support the user's admission or funding for a master's program.

questions.title: What is the exact essay prompt or question?
questions.description: Identify the specific prompt or question the scholarship requires the applicant to answer, so the essay directly addresses what is being asked.

questions.title: What field and program are you applying to?
questions.description: Determine the academic discipline and master's program name so the essay uses the right framing, terminology, and examples.

questions.title: What is the word or character limit for the essay?
questions.description: Establish the length constraint so the draft is structured correctly from the start and does not need major cuts or expansions.

questions.title: What key experiences or achievements should be highlighted?
questions.description: Gather the user's most relevant academic, professional, or personal accomplishments so the essay reflects their real story and stands out.

questions.title: What does the scholarship committee prioritise — merit, need, or impact?
questions.description: Understand the committee's stated or implied selection criteria so the essay emphasises the right qualities and angles.

questions.title: Should the tone be formal and academic or personal and narrative-driven?
questions.description: Clarify the preferred writing style so the essay's voice matches what the user feels comfortable with and what suits the scholarship.

questions.title: When is the application deadline?
questions.description: Establish the submission date to set the right pace for drafting, feedback, and revisions.
